name: [VAP] Voter Registration Team
subject: Not much time left ahead of deadlines
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Here's the deal, team: Voter registration is critical as we barrel towards the deadlines ahead of Election Day.
There's no better way to defend our fundamental right to vote than by registering a ton of new voters and winning critical local, state, and federal elections. Our access to the ballot -- from vote-by-mail to drop boxes to early voting and more -- depends on being able to pass laws that are pro-voter, not pro-incumbent politician.
As little as $3 supports our work to register a new voter. Please, RUSH $30 or more right now to help us register 10 new voters to fight back at the polls >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080626_3&amount=30]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
MS NOW: ‘The largest investment ever’: DNC launches voter registration drive [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080626_3&amount=30]
The 2025 elections showed us a valuable truth, folks: Voter participation is increasing in all the right ways.
Voter registration activity increased across the country. According to the team at National Voter Registration Day, New York recorded more registrations for their 2025 events than in 2024, and California saw similar increases. Earlier this fall it looked like voter participation was going to make a real jump, even in a so-called "off-year".
Then Election Day came. New Jersey had more voters turn out for a gubernatorial election than they had in 20 years. Crucial counties in Pennsylvania saw their highest turnout levels in almost 15 years. New York City reached a turnout percentage unseen in over five decades.
We can drive even higher levels of participation when voters understand the stakes and feel like their vote matters , just like it did last November. That's why our voter registration efforts are so important, and why we work on it all year long.
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. Will you step up with $30 or more today to help register 10 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080626_3&amount=30]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080626_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080626_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080626_3&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080626_3&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080626_3&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080626_3&amount=36]
The key is getting young people -- a major target of opponents of voting rights across the country -- to see the importance of voting now more than ever. Pundits in Virginia said they could have called the election results when they saw the first turnout numbers from the major college campus locations around the state. That's the kind of impact these young voters can have.
Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed the last few years.
The upcoming midterm election will determine whether our democracy stays mired in the darkness and conspiracy theories we hear every day or if we can reclaim our rights -- from voting to choice and more -- and march forward to a better future.
New voter registration -- at a cost to us of just about $3 per new voter -- can be game-changing. Can you pitch in with $30 or however much you can to help us register a tidal wave of new voters ahead of this year's voter registration deadlines? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080626_3&amount=30]
Thank you,
Voter Action Project's Registration Team
https://voteractionproject.org/ [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=080626_3&amount=20]
Donate Now [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=080626_3&amount=20]

name: Chris Pappas
subject: Azerbaijan
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Friend,
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_mcbride_20260806-2.N25APt&refcode=em20260806-3649&t=1&akid=3649%2E21716%2Eao8Swv)
_Josh Rogers/NHPR_
In the GOP primary debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken restaurant."
He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.
**I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.**
My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter — because they do.
**John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life.** He was born into the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan that sells minerals to China.
That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”
New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is running to protect people like himself. **I'm running for everyone else.**
He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he doesn’t represent us. [**If you can, please split a donation between my campaign and Sarah McBride.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_mcbride_20260806-2.N25APt&refcode=em20260806-3649&t=2&akid=3649%2E21716%2Eao8Swv)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_mcbride_20260806-2.N25APt&amount=5&refcode=em20260806-3649&t=21&akid=3649%2E21716%2Eao8Swv)**
John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.
**I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.**
— Chris Pappas
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_mcbride_20260806-2.N25APt&refcode=em20260806-3649&t=22&akid=3649%2E21716%2Eao8Swv)

# **Jonny’s Team Needs** _**YOU**_**🫵**
---
| | Hi Friend,
There are 69 days left until mail-in ballots are sent, 76 days left until early voting, and 90 days until Election Day! Our district is 22,067 square miles. Chip in to help me get our message out before the clock runs out!
The website has been updated to feature our newsletters and a countdown timer.

---
| [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/12Qrw0560DI?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=ogkqYrB4EZqa7qnwMrv1aMdDLbjpvFZcJ9U8gUQtPxn10TGkO_T4MANgqUkS)

## Upcoming This Week
---
|
---
| |
#### **Come meet me in person**

Friday, August 7th
* Hot August Nights - Hosted by Tooele County Democrats. [RSVP here](https://us.list-manage.com/CzHh98t91YL?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=AMvyJJlD21f5MdUTLpUAp_CZQ2YIre0E3pTOkmIWggyQpFXDbLc3YEul7KJ6)

Sunday, August 9th
* Dem Bones - Utah Stonewall Democrats Annual BBQ. [RSVP here](https://us.list-manage.com/cePPy8i1FAV?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=w83MBeI-DGmVXj5MUsgGL-Q1otYWBAYrOCGX6WxvrVxiSDtx_RaqyLuz97gQ)

---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
## What we need & what we did this week
---
|
---
| |
### Volunteers
---
| | Working for a campaign is challenging. Even more so when you are donating your time.
We need to fill some specialty roles as well as have volunteers to accompany us for events, town halls, and canvassers to phone bank and door knock. This is an **ALL HANDS ON DECK** request!
Send an email to [Maria](mailto:volunteer@jonnyutah4congress.com?subject=Interested%20in%20volunteering%20for%20Jonny%20Larsen&body=Full%20name%2C%20phone%2C%20county%20and%20city%20you%20live%20in.%0A%0APlease%20share%20where%20you%20think%20you%20could%20best%20help%20volunteer%20for%20our%20campaign.%20No%20prior%20experience%20is%20needed%20but%20if%20you%20have%20it%2C%20please%20share!), our volunteer coordinator, to find out more.
---
|
---
| |
### KSVC 980AM Radio Interview
---
| | Last week I had a another great interview on KSVC 980AM in Sevier County. You can listen to it on their [website here](https://us.list-manage.com/tjhsfzkbsiE?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=hNGIKnlPIRrO7LgGK4BhRdu45hHuVBZfDADY2XNhWdPSw2OCJbilrw-MXn97). It is listed in the July 2026 section.
After the radio interview, I was joined by the Sevier County Democratic Party at Richfield Park. I met with residents who came for the county’s free lunch program, Summer Lunch in the Park. I spoke with many of them, including a gentleman who aspires to make it to his 100th birthday. He has 6 more years to go. We had a great conversation, and he told me that he use to ride a horse to school.
---
| |
### The Devastating Fires
---
| | Rep. Mike Kennedy recently blamed the U.S. Forest Service for not doing their jobs well enough to fight these fires. In 2025 when he voted to pass the BBB, Kennedy and the rest of our Utah delegation exacerbated this problem. Visit my FaceBook post to read about how he voted to cut funds and staff that ultimately lead to the dire situation we face.
This past Monday evening, I attended the Widemouth 2 Fire Community Meeting in Millard County to hear updates about the fire that has now spread to Sevier County. I am thankful for and praise our firefighters who are working long and tiring shifts to keep everyone safe. They are fighting an uphill battle right now, risking their lives for everyone impacted. A service and self sacrifice for which I have the utmost respect.
Here are some photos from the Widemouth 2 Fire Community Meeting in Millard County.[https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1JLmkckXN1/](https://us.list-manage.com/cWNLTTMGmkP?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=K-6O3uT28o1UlryayBpSKS3nQBSt7LZKQyFWTLExIMFGCdIPo04Gk7HE8IL6)
---
| |
### I Scream For Representation
---
| | Thank you to everyone who joined us for ice cream and discussion. I met new supporters who are eager and excited to join and support the campaign. I got a lot of great feedback from everyone about what is most important to them and their representation in Washington, D.C.
A huge shout out to La Vonne for hosting and to our campaign volunteers for making this event possible. Without you, it would not have been the success it was. I appreciate everything you do. From the bottom of my heart, thank you!
---

Peter, I went back and forth on if I should send you this or not. Not because I didn't know what to say, but because I knew how much it would hurt to say it. It’s difficult to admit that I can't do this alone. [**There's so much weighing on me right now, and finding the right words feels impossible. But I'm trusting these words will reach you the way they need to.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/Ip-uSnF8KkAwrv0GIuY5iMMnr_5_PciRsOSwPJFlEs3in2IKzoodIp0QoOuxiKkRsOAHfNCbtSoew-Y0Pm7XeDOsf1-vuT2wKp8aozsj1E3hQRG2r5hyJoW8-Y-1XngZyfSh8NzBHGHadJu_SOF0_2yx1bdYIy9_lD5o85-UxaOIhJW9GvEOOVPPZ3ramCYGwag5wZbf77Ri1_pk68TYCUT_bk_1N_UVx6NV3kXYxO6nrLaNAtjJ1T-sGkiICVMf7YVqvJos_rsneLx6AsZxCqM4psocPdlwEi0rAv2X90MRWFe38G_VKYPRQ6GajTZHrnDX28jOv05mSSyqxP6NJ9NPP24SUv7dPtiFjWJEU23nbScAhW0WEEwlx1DjOGmBUiFcskGyTbWcJtcYgDLPWKWw7-C3WZ_C5Fpi1N3z4AiV96r0F4mG8PWFTjlAipFGTBD6bqs7n_oNEgpk-GVlIKqew6GgVH7d84ImHV-2BKdjFwXF9o2KEIu7CQzwgwR1ewXIBefGDd5a7fTaMFJ9_Axmn2FwEHMy1-T_NgZkeDcwFhWhudlNHQqWzSle8tegIQJZ3XpVqtOygE5MoOyyi3ZruGlvi2IzBxXHgHFWWR0KpzA3ZACCIl0-3fGxwnMnpVgqirLYAEIe9-q68FHv-lvai66voRLizoo9idbmf511K53QN931Sq2mxofT8ujYnpQxZ_inc5qSafNpZKKMcxhwXQj9FXEyOj3PRjjPorVC2Ucfwn9BRHrsS3S6-4ee9FFQw8--7ry0tFN29LDj1YGPIHdOGyqqFxWxYbVc4nojrg4/hP9x_R8VxtGajvF7bi4BS3Y1XnmuMtAm/23) It’s Congressman Brandon Gill. Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. clean_body: Taking back Texas this year is in our sights. | | | | Derek — I need you to sit with this number for a second: one point. That's it. That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News. In nearly twelve years as governor, through three elections, Greg Abbott has never faced a poll this close. Not once. His campaign has already spent over $54 million this cycle just to hang on to power. This poll says people aren’t buying what he’s selling anymore. Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Nearly 4 in 10 Texans say inflation is the top issue on their minds — and after 12 years of Greg Abbott, they're done waiting around for things to get better. I'm not surprised. I've been hearing it at every stop — from Brownsville to Austin to Amarillo. Families are tired of watching their grocery bills and insurance premiums climb while Abbott hands billions to his donors. This 1-point poll shows that a new chapter for Texas is finally in reach. But it’s not guaranteed. Turnout will decide this election. And Abbott's team knows it — they're going to spend the next 89 days doing everything they can to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up to the polls to vote. They will do anything to keep Texans from turning the page on his failed administration. I can't outspend Greg Abbott, and I don’t need to. Our campaign can out-organize him, but that takes people like you stepping up right now to raise the resources we need to win this race. | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Gina Hinojosa and Battleground Wisconsin will process immediately: | | | | | | We've never been this close. GOTV tour taking Wisconsin by storm
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260806-3125)
Peter,
We’re two days into our statewide get-out-the-vote tour, and the energy on the trail is electric.
People are showing up in the middle of the workday and packing rooms. Wisconsin is ready for a governor who will fight to raise wages, lower property taxes, guarantee universal child care and make life more affordable for working people.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&refcode=em20260806-3125&t=1&akid=3125%2E105371%2E8DSeOk)
We had standing room only in Chippewa Falls. More than 100 people joined us in New Richmond, 75 in River Falls, 80 in Platteville, 120 in Viroqua and 150 in La Crosse. At some stops, we’ve even had to change venues because so many people are showing up.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&refcode=em20260806-3125&t=2&akid=3125%2E105371%2E8DSeOk)
This is what momentum looks like. This is what a winning campaign looks like.
We’re hitting more stops tomorrow and throughout the weekend, and we’re going to carry this energy all the way into Tuesday’s primary. But we need the resources to keep our organizers on the road, reach every voter we can and finish this campaign strong.
**[Will you chip in $10, $25 or whatever you can today to fuel our final get-out-the-vote push?](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&refcode=em20260806-3125&t=3&akid=3125%2E105371%2E8DSeOk)**
We’ve built something powerful together. Now let’s bring it home.
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&amount=5&refcode=em20260806-3125&t=6&akid=3125%2E105371%2E8DSeOk)**
With gratitude,
Fran

Peter,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

clean_body: | Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 2 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult few weeks. name: Deb HQ
subject: The July rundown for you
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=1&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
# **4th of July/ Las Vegas Fiestas Parade**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=2&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Las Vegas, New Mexico came together to celebrate the Fourth of July as Deb joined community members in honoring the people and traditions that make our state and our country so special. From those who have served our nation to the neighbors who strengthen their communities every day, the spirit of service is what makes New Mexico proud. Deb was honored to celebrate our country's birthday alongside New Mexicans.
---
|
---
# **Meow Wolf**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=3&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Meow Wolf continues to showcase New Mexico’s nationally recognized creative economy and the artists whose work attracts visitors from around the world. Arts and cultural organizations play a vital role in supporting tourism, creating jobs, and helping local businesses thrive. Deb believes investing in New Mexico's creative industries strengthens communities, grows our economy, and preserves the culture that makes our state unlike anywhere else.
---
|
---
# **Sandoval Indivisible**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=4&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb joined Sandoval County Indivisible and Representative Kathleen Cates for a community conversation focused on the issues that matter most to New Mexicans. Hearing directly from voters remains central to Deb's campaign as communities continue sharing their priorities, including lowering costs, strengthening public education, expanding access to healthcare, improving public safety, and protecting civil liberties. Deb believes strong leadership starts with showing up, listening, and delivering results for New Mexicans.
---
|
---
# **Tricore Labs**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=5&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At TriCore Reference Laboratories, Deb toured one of New Mexico's largest clinical laboratory organizations and learned more about the essential role laboratory professionals play in delivering high-quality healthcare. Reliable diagnostic testing is critical to early detection, timely treatment, and better health outcomes for patients across the state. Deb remains committed to strengthening New Mexico's healthcare workforce and expanding access to quality, affordable care in every community.
---
|
---
# **New Mexico Tattoo Fiesta**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=6&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At the New Mexico Tattoo Fiesta, Deb celebrated the incredible artistry and creativity of tattoo artists whose work reflects the rich culture and diversity of our state. The event highlights the talent, craftsmanship, and self-expression that continue to shape New Mexico's vibrant creative community. Deb was proud to celebrate an art form that tells personal stories, honors individual identity, and showcases the creativity found across New Mexico.
---
|
---
# South Valley **Growers'** Market
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=7&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb visited the South Valley Growers' Market to meet with local farmers, growers, and small business owners who help power New Mexico's economy. She knows that supporting local agriculture means protecting our land and water, strengthening rural communities, and creating opportunities for small businesses to thrive. Investing in New Mexico's farmers and entrepreneurs is an important part of building a stronger, more resilient economy for communities across the state.
---
|
---
# **Lowrider Day on the Santa Fe Plaza**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=8&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb joined New Mexicans in celebrating one of the state's most cherished traditions at Lowrider Day in Santa Fe. Rooted in generations of history, lowrider culture reflects the artistry, craftsmanship, music, and community that make New Mexico unique. Deb believes preserving and celebrating traditions like these honors our shared heritage and helps ensure New Mexico's rich culture continues to thrive for generations to come.
---
|
---
# **Adelante Development Center**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=9&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At Adelante Development Center, Deb met with staff to learn more about the organization's work connecting adults with disabilities to employment, training, and essential support services. Adelante plays an important role in helping New Mexicans with disabilities gain meaningful employment, build independence, and access the support they need to thrive. Deb is committed to ensuring organizations like these have the resources they need to continue their vital work.
---
|
---
# **Midtown Arts and Design Alliance (MADA) of New Mexico**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=10&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At the Midtown Arts and Design Alliance (MADA), Deb visited a collaborative hub bringing together artists, entrepreneurs, educators, and community organizations. By transforming underused space into a center for arts, education, and innovation, MADA is helping create new opportunities for local businesses and creatives. Deb believes collaborative spaces like MADA help create stronger, more connected communities across New Mexico.
---
|
---
# **New Mexico School Boards Leadership Retreat**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=11&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At the New Mexico School Boards Leadership Retreat, Deb joined school board members from across the state to discuss the opportunities and challenges facing New Mexico's public schools. She knows that preparing students for success starts with investing in teachers, expanding career and technical education, improving early literacy, and giving every community the flexibility to meet the unique needs of its students. As governor, Deb will work to ensure every child has access to a high-quality public education, no matter where they live.
---
|
---
# **Embudo Valley Library**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=12&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At the Embudo Valley Library, Deb heard about the work being done through the New Mexico Rural Library Initiative to support rural communities across the state. Rural libraries provide essential resources beyond traditional library services, including early childhood literacy programs, community support services, and access to information and opportunities on jobs, healthcare, and economic development. As governor, Deb will prioritize investments in rural communities and the organizations that provide essential services to the people who call them home.
---
|
---
# **Celebrating Route 66’s 100th birthday at Summerfest**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=13&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb joined community members at Route 66 Summerfest to celebrate the 100th anniversary of one of New Mexico's most iconic landmarks. Route 66 has long been a symbol of freedom, connection, culture, and economic opportunity, bringing together generations of New Mexicans and visitors from around the world.
---
|
---
# **Taos Parade**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=14&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
At the Taos Parade, Deb celebrated with New Mexicans during one of the community’s most historic annual traditions. Parade season is a chance to recognize the people, places, and stories that make towns across New Mexico unique. Deb was proud to celebrate alongside the Taos community and the families who keep these traditions alive.
---
|
---
# **Speridian Technologies**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=15&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Innovation is creating opportunity right here in New Mexico. It was great to visit Speridian Technologies and see how they’re creating high-quality jobs and investing in our state’s workforce. At Speridian Technologies, Deb learned more about the company's work to create high-quality jobs and use technology to solve complex challenges for businesses. Speridian's investment in New Mexico reflects the importance of innovation and workforce development in building a stronger economy. Deb believes that supporting innovation, growing the workforce, and partnering with businesses that invest in New Mexico is how we create more opportunity and build a stronger economy for every New Mexican.
---
|
---
# **Fiestas**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=16&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Throughout July, Deb celebrated with communities at the Española, Mora, and Chimayó fiestas. These celebrations honor the traditions, culture, and community spirit that have been passed down for generations. Deb was proud to join families across Northern New Mexico and celebrate the people and traditions that make our state unlike anywhere else.
---
|
---
# **Santa Fe Spanish Market**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=17&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb spent the day at the Santa Fe Spanish Market celebrating the artists and traditions that continue to shape New Mexico’s culture. Every piece at the Spanish Market tells a story of tradition, family, and generations of craftsmanship. Deb remains committed to supporting New Mexico's artists and preserving the cultural traditions that make the state unique.
---
|
---
# **American Postal Workers Union (APWU) Albuquerque Local 380 Picket Line**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=18&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb joined postal workers on the picket line to hear directly about the challenges they're facing and the importance of protecting the Postal Service. The Postal Service connects rural communities, delivers lifesaving medications, supports small businesses, and ensures every family can stay connected no matter where they live. Deb is committed to being a leader who will protect good union jobs and defend the public services New Mexicans rely on.
---
|
---
# **Stephanie Garcia Richard Wins Democratic Lieutenant Governor Nomination**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=19&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
After winning the Democratic State Central Committee election, Stephanie Garcia Richard officially became the Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor. Deb believes Stephanie is the right person for the job because she has spent her career delivering for New Mexicans. Together, they bring experienced, proven leadership and a shared commitment to lowering costs, strengthening schools, expanding access to healthcare, and ensuring our communities are safe.
---
**Endorsements:** **Senator Joseph Cervantes** **Senator George Munoz** **Senator Antonio “Moe” Maestas**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/9563?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=20&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
# **KTAO Interview**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=21&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb joined Paddy Mac on the KTAOS Morning Show to discuss her vision for New Mexico’s future. She spoke about the challenges and opportunities facing communities across New Mexico, including safeguarding our water resources, cutting red tape for business owners, and creating more opportunities statewide. Deb believes every New Mexican deserves the opportunity to hear directly from their leaders and have their voices heard in return.
---
|
---
# **Governor Gretchen Whitmer on Substack**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15615?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=22&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb joined Governor Gretchen Whitmer for a conversation about what it takes to lead a state, why she's running for governor, and the importance of delivering results for working families. They also discussed the challenges facing states today and the value of experienced leadership that puts people first.
---
|
---
# KOAT
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=23&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
On KOAT, Deb joined newly elected Democratic lieutenant governor nominee Stephanie Garcia Richard for their first joint interview, where they shared their vision for building a stronger New Mexico. Together, they discussed their commitment to lowering costs for working families, expanding access to affordable healthcare, strengthening public schools, protecting programs New Mexicans rely on, and delivering results that improve lives in every corner of the state.
---
|
---
# Source New Mexico
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15613?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=24&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
In _Source New Mexico's_ article, "_New Mexico Dem Governor Nominee Haaland Reiterates Plans to Overhaul State Child Welfare Agency,_ " Deb outlined her plan to overhaul CYFD by restoring accountability, rebuilding public trust, strengthening services for children and families, and creating a system that prioritizes children's safety and well-being. She stressed that New Mexico's children deserve a child welfare system that helps lift them up.
---
|
---
# Chaco Canyon
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15616?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&t=25&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---
Deb submitted a public comment in strong support of permanently protecting the 10-mile buffer zone surrounding Chaco Canyon, calling the Trump administration's effort to dismantle these protections outrageous. Giving New Mexicans and Tribal communities just seven days to weigh in on a decision that could permanently impact one of the world's most significant cultural and archaeological landscapes is unacceptable and fails to respect meaningful public and Tribal consultation.

In her statement, Deb reaffirmed that she has always fought to protect New Mexico's sacred and public lands. As Secretary of the Interior, she established the 10-mile protective buffer around Chaco Canyon to help safeguard Tribal cultural resources and thousands of irreplaceable archaeological sites from new oil and gas drilling. She remains committed to defending these protections and ensuring Chaco Canyon and the surrounding sacred landscapes are preserved for future generations.

---
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---
|
* * *
| | [Donate >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1167-ot-nd&amount=5&t=26&akid=11576%2E400544%2Ep4Vbuc)
---

Deb believes every New Mexican deserves the opportunity to hear directly from their leaders and have their voices heard in return. | Governor Gretchen Whitmer on Substack Deb joined Governor Gretchen Whitmer for a conversation about what it takes to lead a state, why she's running for governor, and the importance of delivering results for working families. They also discussed the challenges facing states today and the value of experienced leadership that puts people first. | KOAT On KOAT, Deb joined newly elected Democratic lieutenant governor nominee Stephanie Garcia Richard for their first joint interview, where they shared their vision for building a stronger New Mexico. Together, they discussed their commitment to lowering costs for working families, expanding access to affordable healthcare, strengthening public schools, protecting programs New Mexicans rely on, and delivering results that improve lives in every corner of the state. | Source New Mexico In Source New Mexico's article, "New Mexico Dem Governor Nominee Haaland Reiterates Plans to Overhaul State Child Welfare Agency, " Deb outlined her plan to overhaul CYFD by restoring accountability, rebuilding public trust, strengthening services for children and families, and creating a system that prioritizes children's safety and well-being. She stressed that New Mexico's children deserve a child welfare system that helps lift them up. | Chaco Canyon Deb submitted a public comment in strong support of permanently protecting the 10-mile buffer zone surrounding Chaco Canyon, calling the Trump administration's effort to dismantle these protections outrageous. Giving New Mexicans and Tribal communities just seven days to weigh in on a decision that could permanently impact one of the world's most significant cultural and archaeological landscapes is unacceptable and fails to respect meaningful public and Tribal consultation. In her statement, Deb reaffirmed that she has always fought to protect New Mexico's sacred and public lands. As Secretary of the Interior, she established the 10-mile protective buffer around Chaco Canyon to help safeguard Tribal cultural resources and thousands of irreplaceable archaeological sites from new oil and gas drilling. She remains committed to defending these protections and ensuring Chaco Canyon and the surrounding sacred landscapes are preserved for future generations. | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | |

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Breaking news, Peter:

Justice Democrat Justin J. Pearson just handily won the Democratic primary
in Tennessee’s 9th congressional district!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260806-3-jjp.nuDr1v&refcode=em20260806-38141&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38141%2E1203867%2EJbr1te ]Graphic: Congratulations TN-09 Primary 2026 Winner Justin J. Pearson

Now, as our TENTH 2026 candidate to move forward from the primaries,
Justin will advance to the November 3rd general election as the official
Democratic nominee for this open House seat.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260806-3-jjp.nuDr1v&refcode=em20260806-38141&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=38141%2E1203867%2EJbr1te ]He’ll face off against a far-right Republican who is already getting
thousands bundled by AIPAC, so we can’t waste a moment: will you rush
$10 to help us defeat MAGA and send Justin to Congress?

When he first launched his campaign, Justin set out to challenge
Do-Nothing Democrat Rep. Steve Cohen for this seat. But when Donald Trump
directed the Republican-led state legislature to use the newly gutted
Voting Rights Act to gerrymander the only Black-majority district in TN
out of existence, Cohen wasn’t willing to fight and dropped out.

Justin could have thrown in the towel and walked away, but he didn’t.
Instead, he recommitted himself to running in the newly redrawn TN-09
district with a clear vision to unite disenfranchised voters across race
and class to take on billionaire oligarchs making life unaffordable and
MAGA fascists trying to turn the clock back on our basic rights.

That’s who Justin is: a fighter. When Democratic voters talk about needing
‘fighters’ in Congress, they mean leaders like him, who in the face of
billionaire-backed Jim Crow refuse to surrender their community’s voice
and power.

As an organizer, he led a coalition that successfully stopped a
multibillion-dollar crude oil pipeline project that would have poisoned
Memphis’s drinking water and stolen land from South Memphis residents.

He went on to become the second-youngest member of the Tennessee General
Assembly. In 2023, he was one of three Democratic lawmakers, known as the
‘Tennessee Three,’ who were expelled by Republicans for bravely protesting
gun violence on the House floor after a tragic mass school shooting.

Even now as he’s running for Congress, Justin’s fighting to stop Elon
Musk’s xAI data centers from polluting and poisoning his community for
profit.

And when Republicans gerrymandered his district, he went on a 15-county
tour of every new county in TN-09 to meet every voter where they were at.

Justice Democrats helped Justin build and launch his campaign last October
as a day-one endorser and key adviser. With your support, we raised over
$68,000 directly for his campaign from more than 1,885 grassroots donors,
with an average contribution of $36.

Like the rest of our slate, Justin is ready to go to Washington to vote
for Medicare for All, ending U.S. military aid to Israel, banning data
centers, restoring voting rights, and holding corporate interests
accountable to the working class.

But to get there, he needs to win the next battle on November 3rd against
the full weight of the Republican machine.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260806-3-jjp.nuDr1v&refcode=em20260806-38141&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1004&akid=38141%2E1203867%2EJbr1te ]Fuel our fight to the general election: make a split contribution of
any amount to Justice Democrats and Justin’s campaign to help us get him
over the final finish line in less than 3 months.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260806-3-jjp.nuDr1v&refcode=em20260806-38141&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1023&akid=38141%2E1203867%2EJbr1te ]Contribute $10

Thank you for everything you’ve done to support our work to help Justin
and nine other bold progressives win their primaries in this historic
election cycle.

Our fight’s not over, so let’s keep it up!

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas

When I first went to Congress, I thought that if I worked hard enough, I could find a way to contribute to the passage of major legislation. To me, the problem was the incumbents, who found it easy to do nothing and blame their opponents. I still think that's true, but it's more of a symptom than a cause. A more significant cause for our stagnant politics is explained in a book I recently came across, which has the benefit of being both short and thorough:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6a5bb902-5e1e-4680-86c8-829a4892c702?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Hyperpolitics](https://substack.com/redirect/74c30ec0-dee6-4e19-ac2d-b4c1a3e2b144?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Anton Jager "[is being devoured by the left](https://substack.com/redirect/224c3c69-a1f0-465c-a59e-237203ee3094?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" in Europe and the United States, but it should interest people across the spectrum. Jager's basic thesis is that we live in an era of high politicization -- lots of people vote, there are mass protests, and politics seems to occupy more and more of our attention -- but low institutionalization. By institutionalization he means "civic affiliation and membership," drawing on the Putnam literature I mentioned [last week](https://substack.com/redirect/72edd333-0fd3-490c-87b5-7043466f7da6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Politics are "hyper" now because they're always happening in our minds, but out there in the world, so little seems to be happening. By comparison, the era of "mass politics" following WWII featured both high politicization and high institutionalization (and I'd add, high accomplishment), and "post politics" in the 1990s was low on both. (Jager would say that "accomplishment" in post-politics occurred outside of the democratic process, mostly at the level of unelected actors like central banks.)
Had I read this in 2018, I might have realized that the performance of the House of Representatives was being driven as much by changes in society as it was by the attitudes of its own members: ...

## Senate Panel Holds Fauci in Contempt
A Senate committee voted along party lines Thursday to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in [contempt of Congress](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3OpDAMBuDTQBdkMiGBIsU2dLPtligkDngVEgTeQXP7FSPNCb7Okn_k5_3znJ6OEuXlt9vQcixTxutMyIzHFN0_TyumQNmXzLjtvGBGDJMEqQX0AswUHKX3pOpgI6LER422Nb2GwahuqFcb51mh9sH3gOGhlZJ9jEZDp4OO0bia7H0NejAttND1jUGvhhbVrMMc9QCVAgzE5Wj-Fsq8Ykzv8sKj8WWrk12Z97N6_KrkWMnxuq4mz_5W3P1KjntJxOTPSo6-5OXA8y5PzI7LcYpXYRRruZGLcJnXkt_iIxdftPjuiT2h-wxGirwKFofPrhtg6Lv6sGG_KCU6takULJuj9HmRf5Try8r_AQAA__9eo5CP) after the former COVID-19 czar took the Fifth 111 times rather than answer questions about lockdowns, pandemic origins, and gain-of-function research funding. Separately, three Republican attorneys general in Florida, West Virginia, and Louisiana are [investigating whether](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd4wwxjAuKNK427QpLQwP8yIMI_N2HP995I3yBdsfHd17fn0sHw4zlu2n28FSrEuBs2UggmOJ7tNjghyw-FoI9hdtUADCIoXUXDy5MEtwmK9FdcFGAAlDB7Y3Ty0mo8apS3ZwgzKT9l7rsY9-DD6ObgAh4-r70MsO7W0TT2F60Yvx-TDg1dSDWnVYo54EUwICUj0evysWShDzVd9wPHzdu2wT0aux4QeTM5PzeZ6P07WEZaNa4I_bsfxDmZxfNaO_mJwTuEzJuwOYnJU2Rg6ayblBcQT8XQl4qvfvjbtCqZaLf8Xg_zvwRjeJ5Q2NcHOEtTS-fq5rvpXdYcPrxJyxacOU2HaH-WsvfSvy28q_AQAA__8AG5SZ) Fauci personally profited from his own pandemic guidance, and this week subpoenaed his records dating back to January 2020. Among their targets is the nearly $1 million [Dan David Prize](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL_upSAQhZ8Gu7lB_AMWFNvY_bbd0qAMyAbBwHhvfPuN9xW2mUxyki_nO39-lh8TYkj-tzlQk8tLwk-NSIRlcebawo7RhrTlRHic5DEh2kVwMQJXwOViTYj30jdWO0SBXYO6lWrkk-yHqdn1ZnBVUuLgJumMEijXybl1ENb1XedUE_RD44rLlrd8UC-JWz-12K-jXd04cdZztIFyef3NIdGOLt75jeW15aOJeic6K-t-MTEzMaf7zJWeiIn5ATMxc_Wc57sqPH5MzLaASbTndMNXE-q1nhmTQQvrDbQXRPD5hEqGEIyv4HIBEyN6tPGGs2QXKCQP2TnY8jtYaCfwV7AmbcjE3BRtz0-IMdRRsp77w4T4LU3_tfRbi38BAAD__3QZlBU) he collected in 2021. Emails show he solicited the nomination and supplied the materials for the prize himself. _"Congratulations ... you're rich!"_ his personal assistant wrote when the money came through. A preemptive pardon from former President Biden shields Fauci from federal charges through January 2025, but the state investigations fall outside its reach. Chairman Rand Paul is [routing the referral](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LvO4yAUBOCnsTssTHwtKLZxl223tLgc4hNhQHBiNm-_SqR9gr8eaTTf_Lnvd4Uew-O3OkGSi3uAWjwQQd6dehk8wFsMJgaCM9EDAoDdBRcT4wvj824V-vc-tFY6AAG3FmQ_LxNf52Fc20MKrR2oUYxiUOvUj4vTrrfCCM1NP-tbi_LTxhc-97zn49LNYIa1h0FPVrtp5c3AwSLF3D0jBjrA-Xe8IHcmnq2XB1Eqze1XI7ZGbLXWzsW_H8Unb8SWokdCUxqxZRUsS-rlWcpg0VBhXyP7z2NXJGBJlcKuWAsrFR0xG58sg4OclW-ztKmi91imuRn441Tov0voR_ddUvwLAAD__3gWh-M) straight to prosecutors through Vice President JD Vance, skipping a full Senate vote.

The Fathom rides on Ford's new Universal Electric Vehicle platform, built at its [Louisville, Kentucky, plant](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdKDFMQYKF39Dl7-9Ehl7HfZibOQsQXn7E_cK14xGGukb6fu6z3dLkdLjv93QcMhzwvMVkRnLHOzhaMXoKbmcGLedH5gQ_SxB6hqGGvrZW4qfWVXeBESJtwpN2w8axl51Y7WaFjoJKihnx-BbNfiAWkqll1GFTrtbReaiwQB9Cy10Q9OjU2OLatF-CXoEoQA9cS7Nd6bEK4b4yW8sjctbFc3KvL_E7Z-Qk5DTeZ6NS4u7RiGnCy3kBMMVVwu5-DpYXvNW7-Sex15zOdyz3gs5bFbeYlWM30-KkV66Fwoem6X4e8Z_MvQ28icAAP__LUt4_g), and comes standard with BlueCruise hands-free highway driving, bidirectional power capable of running a home, and Apple Maps built into the touchscreen. There's just one catch: Ford hasn't actually shown the truck yet, and [won't reveal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O4yAUhZ8Gd0TX-AdcUGzjLttuaZHLJbCDIcI3ifL2I88rTHN0pCN9R_r-XberSzmV-1-3k-VQt0LvIxMztS24J6ZI2aeCtTDtD75TIfKbAjVLMBL05l3Kn23svA1EioaObK_NDIsep6WLNgzGOO16MBrHBZxeSKnFBUSYQrhhl-xJAwO6hx4mc9GE49LTeJv9LcwLiBHIJ67t8r-mwpFC_tQXtQvWvcs2Mj8OMfwRahVqZcKI7VkwnrNQ6wkXagVzxtlCbf6Qhd6SMiG3hJLbE79kcBzrLg92jQ_pWCozTCDU2jXrH--UczpmLUa47y7ln3f-lbKXVd8BAAD__8LFfrM) what the Fathom looks like until preorders open in early 2027. The launch is the company's big bet after losing $19.5 billion on earlier EV programs.
## Buc-ee's Called a Trademark Bully
Buc-ee's has sued [more than a dozen](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu4yAURVeDO6IHdsAuKKZxl2mntDA8zMtgiAxOlN1_JVv49b06Rzr_bsvNUqK8_bU7mhbKkvFVE7aGxxLs6Shi8pRdyQ33R9swI_pFglQcRg568ZbSexk6bwKixL5DI_SoYNLDdeqisdOKo_DCSw0CriO44HonVzWIfgyIHZkPDUbQ4nu4aHTDJHBYlV-DmoANgJ5aOS73QrlFDOldnnhcXNm7ZGJrj8r6P0zOTM4tYqSUPhuT83pWylgrk7MCUFoAX0_HESuvJ1ZeIhXuoqXM7yVmXhI98eDJ1sZfiP95K5m22Jicu8P4x4tSoqo0G2DbLX01XftVt6eRPwEAAP__HhOCbA) businesses over its buck-toothed beaver, going after companies with cartoon animal mascots and names that end in an "ee's" sound. The latest fight is in Georgia, where Buc-ee's sued a convenience store called Teddy's Market over its [cartoon bear](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLvupCAYxZ8GOswng4AFxTZ2s-2WhsunskExgGPm7TfuK_yrU5zkdy5_3vPbxhSP9bfd0bQlzwfeNWFrWObFXj5umEI8fD4a7mdb8UAMMwcuGWgGag42pu8saDALIscXRdMrLWFUYhjpZrDXLylAAyy8986jGqQfVFBBBze6QKN5aKBB9dDDoDuFXow9CieDW-QIRACG2HLp_uZ4tA2X9M0fLJ3PO01ma-2s5PWL8Inw6b7v7i42PSbh07OG8MmehE_u8oiV1QsrWzGXNVpWWy7IHhpzaB_ZbfW5MXutV23sqUb4RIsJ5x1TilUqImDdbfwfQduPTvsY_i8AAP__8p-Bsw). Both mascots are smiling animals in hats with white eye highlights and a hint of pink tongue, the complaint says. Its owner was blunter: _"If you have a shark coming at you, you are going to punch it in the face."_ The campaign drew a late-night audience in July, when John Oliver launched a "Buc-Off" merch line daring the chain to sue him.
